To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nitro group of 4HADN is reduced in anoxic environments to the nitroso group and that nitrosoarenes are reactive toward biomass and humics, and this reactivity is enhanced in the presence of proteinaceous material.

nitrosoarenes are more reactive with biomass and natural organic material than arylhydroxlamines and the more reduced TNT derivatives containing nitroso functionality are more likely to react than the less reduced ones
The reactivity of TNT metabolites containing nitroso and hydroxylamino moieties toward humic substances and biomass was investigated using model systems and molecular modeling techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of nitrosoarenes and arylhydroxaminos in the environment.
the identification and characterization of the reactive species formed during the sequential bioremediation of TNT.
the reactivity of partially reduced metabolites of TNT toward biomass and natural organic carbon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nitroarene and arylhydroxamino moieties of TNT are not likely to be involved in the formation of stable products with biomass or natural organic matter fractions.
the reductive transformation of TNT in the absence of amines leads to the formation of nitrosoarenes that are capable of reacting with humic substances and biomass.
the nitro and hydroxylamino functionalities of TNT are responsible for the incorporation of TNT residues into biomass and humic acid fractions of a system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of nitroso metabolites of TNT to biomass and humic acid is a significant process and is dependent on the redox state of the nitroarene metabolites.

the nitro group of TNT was more likely to undergo reduction to the hydroxylamine functionality than the nitroso group, and the latter group was more reactive toward nucleophiles than the hydroxylamino functionality.
nitrosoarenes formed during the reduction of TNT can bind to proteins and humic substances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nitro group is the most important moiety in the reactivity of TNT metabolites with natural organic matter and biomass.
arylhydroxaminotoluene and nitroso derivatives of TNT can be removed from aqueous solutions via binding to biomass and humic substances.
the presence of nitroso moities in TNT-derived metabolites is likely to contribute to the incorporation of TNT residues into the biomass and humic fractions of an environment.
